body: One issue with forward searching for `FROM` is that you can find column names containing `from` and also incorrectly generate the list of fields.

Nested statements as column values require parenthesis, don't they?

A simple parser would probably work.  It just needs to scan for a ( or ) and FROM.  If it finds ( increment a counter and start looking for ( or ).  When it finds ), decrement the counter.  If the counter is 0 and you find FROM, you should be safe to parse everything before hand as the column string.

Though it would also have to deal with quoted identifiers to make sure someone didn't name their column FROM.

I can take a stab at this.
I was more thinking about columns like `from_address`. But subqueries in the select clause are another problem.

This issue is also affecting me. Works fine with some of my models and Containable behavior in a limited capacity.

It seems to go pear-shaped with more than 2 models or multiple associations by different name to the same model.

I find the last model in the 'contain' disappears to be replaced with a similar [ModelName" LEFT JOIN "main"] array key in the resultSet.

There are also issues when Containable behavior is used with Paginator->sort() helper. Some models in the 'contain' which were available before sorting by a column disappear in the new sorted resultSet.

I hope CakePHP 2.5.7 is not too far away. I am having to implement all sorts of workarounds (no sort, no contain etc.) to ensure it doesn't break the app.

@trenshaw There is currently no straightfoward fix for SQLite as CakePHP unfortunately needs to munge the queries as the Sqlite2 interface does not give the model layer enough metadata to function correctly. What does your problematic query look like?

Here is my _paginate_ query:

Note 'ToVender' is missing and instead I have a 'Queue" LEFT JOIN "main"' key with a value of '"users" AS "ServiceUser" ON ("Queue"' => 'ValEx' - completely unexpected.

Also to note, my `user.display_name` used to be a _virtualField_ / Sqlite3 concat || of `user.first_name` and `user.last_name` but when used with Containable behavior also got odd results e.g. `User__display_name` as key.

Obviously I have a Application, Service and Vendor model for which I have created my `FromApplication` and `ToApplication` associations etc.

I don't want to have to migrate the app to MySQL as an 'embedded' database is perfect for this type of application given it will live broker-side and not part of the main pool of web and DB servers (being a combination SOAP server/client and MQ consumer).
